paras: The police shooting of Charles Smith took place early on August 7, 1910, at Ninth and Clinton streets in Philadelphia, when Policeman Markey fired on Smith, a Black man, as he ran from an alleged street robbery. Hit by two bullets, Smith was taken to the Pennsylvania Hospital in serious condition and held there under police guard.

According to a Philadelphia dispatch, Markey was standing at the corner of Ninth and Clinton streets when he heard a man shout "Murder!" On the policeman's account, he found a white man "struggling in the grip" of two Black men who were going through his pockets, and both men ran. Markey chased one of them and, as the man gained ground, fired two shots. The man fell, got up and kept running; a third shot was fired, and he ran on until he "dropped insensible."

The wounded man was identified as Charles Smith, who said his home was in Detroit. He lay in the Pennsylvania Hospital with two bullets in his body and a policeman posted on each side of his cot. When police went back to the scene, the man said to have been robbed was gone, and the dispatch names no complainant.
The coverage does not report whether Smith survived, whether he was charged, or whether the second man was caught.

The shooting is known from a single dispatch in the Washington Times of August 7, 1910, printed on page 2. The paper ran it under the headline "Policeman Shoots Fugitive Footpad," with the subhead "Negro, Hit by Two Bullets, Runs Until He Drops Unconscious." The story was told wholly from the police side: it called Smith a "footpad" without qualification and identified both suspects by race against "a white man" as their alleged victim. No account of the shooting was found in the Black press.

reader.title: Police shooting of Charles Smith in Philadelphia
bases: A single policeman shot a fleeing Black man accused of a street robbery; no crowd or mob is mentioned (A1).
Only one dispatch, in the Washington Times, reports the shooting, and its account rests on the police version (A1).

accounts.label: Police account (Philadelphia dispatch)
accounts.gist: Markey heard a cry of 'Murder!', found two Black men going through a white man's pockets, chased one, and fired three shots; the man fell, rose, and ran until he collapsed.

framing.detail: The Washington Times ran the dispatch under 'POLICEMAN SHOOTS FUGITIVE FOOTPAD', treating Smith's guilt as given and marking his race in the subhead, with no comment on the shooting.
